biography:
Marco Pisani, a name whispered with a mix of awe and disdain in the Ligier paddock, hails from the vibrant streets of São Paulo, Brazil. Growing up amidst the roar of modified engines and the scent of burning rubber, Marco's passion for racing ignited early. He began his motorsport journey with karting at the age of 10, quickly establishing himself as a force to be reckoned with. A defining moment came at the Brazilian Karting Championship, where, despite starting last due to a mechanical failure, he clawed his way to victory, showcasing the raw talent and relentless spirit that would define his career.

His transition to single-seaters was meteoric. He dominated the Brazilian Formula Regional series before making the leap to European racing. While success wasn't immediate, his tenacity and undeniable speed caught the eye of the Ligier team. Now, at 24, Marco finds himself at what many consider the peak of his abilities, piloting the Ligier JS P320. He's a flashy personality, both on and off the track, attracting attention wherever he goes. Some find him arrogant, others admire his confidence; but no one can deny his potential.

However, the transition to endurance racing has not been seamless. While flashes of brilliance are evident, consistency remains a challenge. He has struggled to balance his aggressive driving style with the demands of long races, often pushing the car and tires beyond their limits. Despite this, he remains a key member of the Ligier team, constantly working to refine his skills and unlock his full potential. The pressure is on for him to deliver the results his talent promises, turning potential into tangible victories.
drivingStyle: Marco's driving style is characterized by aggressive late braking and a willingness to take risks. He attacks corners with ferocity, often pushing the limits of grip to gain an advantage. While his speed is undeniable, his tire management sometimes suffers due to his aggressive approach. Under pressure, he tends to become even more aggressive, sometimes leading to mistakes. However, when everything clicks, his raw speed and daring maneuvers make him a formidable competitor.

rivalries.name: Jean-Pierre Dubois
rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry stemming from a controversial overtaking maneuver at Le Mans, where Dubois accused Pisani of reckless driving.

rivalries.name: Isabella Rossi
rivalries.reason: A constant battle for position in the championship standings, fueled by their contrasting driving styles (Pisani: aggressive, Rossi: calculated).

rivalries.name: Kenji Tanaka
rivalries.reason: A clash of egos and sponsorship deals, both representing rival watch brands and constantly trying to outdo each other on and off the track.

quirks: Always wears a specific pair of lucky socks, no matter how worn they are.
Listens to the same Brazilian samba song before every race.
Refuses to shake hands with anyone on the grid before the start.
famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser. I'm here to win, and I'll do whatever it takes."
careerHighlight: Winning the Brazilian Karting Championship after starting last, proving his determination and skill to the world.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at the 24 Hours of Daytona due to an unforced error, costing his team a potential victory.
